comments.about: What a parameterless 'npm run auto' does: every model below, one after another, on the 'run' test, each one collected, graded and reset before the next. Flags override any field here, e.g. npm run auto -- --model opus:max --test migrations.
comments.run: The test: 'mcp' (Umbraco MCP server, the main one), 'mcp-guided' (the same build and rubric, with a shorter prompt that ends in numbered steps: for small models, e.g. npm run auto -- --test mcp-guided --model claude-haiku-4-5-20251001,claude-haiku-5-5,gpt-6-luna,gpt-5.6-luna), 'migrations' (C# migration plans) or 'playwright' (driving the backoffice). An array such as ["mcp", "migrations"] runs every model on every test. npm run score ranks each test in its own table, against its own medians.
comments.anthropic.effort: Effort for every model: 'low', 'medium', 'high', 'xhigh' or 'max'. 'default' leaves it to the CLI. Haiku 4.5 has no effort setting and always runs without one (Haiku 5.5 has one).
comments.anthropic.models: Run in this order. Full IDs are pinned, so the sweep means the same thing next month: claude-fable-5-1 (Fable 5.1), claude-opus-5-5 (Opus 5.5), claude-sonnet-5-5 (Sonnet 5.5), claude-sonnet-5 (Sonnet 5), claude-haiku-5-5 (Haiku 5.5, which has auto mode and effort), claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 (Haiku 4.5: no auto mode, no effort; runs with bypassPermissions). Aliases 'fable', 'opus', 'sonnet' and 'haiku' also work but follow whatever is newest. Short forms like 'sonnet-5-5' get 'claude-' added. 'model:effort' overrides the effort for one entry, e.g. 'claude-opus-5-5:max'.
comments.grader: The headless session that follows exam-prompt.md after each run: check, screenshots, grade, reset. Keep it the same across a sweep so the grades compare.
comments.options.permissionMode: Permission mode for both sessions. 'auto' matches the manual runs. Nothing can answer a prompt, so anything that would ask is denied.
comments.options.timeoutMinutes: How long the blog prompt may run before the session is killed.
comments.options.budgetUsd: Optional spending cap per session (claude --max-budget-usd); null for none.
comments.options.codexMaxUsedPercent: A Codex run only starts while the plan's 5-hour window is at most this % used (one run took ~15% on Plus); otherwise it waits for the reset and other models run meanwhile.
comments.openai: Models run through Codex (codex app-server), after the anthropic ones, with the same prompts, MCP servers and grader. Effort: 'low', 'medium', 'high', 'xhigh' or 'max' (most also take 'ultra'). Models on the ChatGPT subscription: gpt-6.1-sol, gpt-6-astra, gpt-6-sol, gpt-6-luna, gpt-5.6-sol, gpt-5.6-terra, gpt-5.6-luna, gpt-5.5. Codex runs with full access and its own automatic reviewer (the closest match to Claude Code's auto mode), with the desktop app's plugins, browser and computer use switched off.
comments.local: Models on this machine, run through Claude Code exactly like a Claude model, after the openai ones: LM Studio serves the model (its Anthropic-compatible /v1/messages endpoint), and the runner starts a small proxy in between that gives the model's chat template one system message (Qwen's raises on Claude Code's mid-conversation system messages). models = the API identifier; lmstudioKeys maps it to LM Studio's model key (lms ls). contextLength is what LM Studio loads it with and what Claude Code is told to compact against: the 160 Umbraco MCP tools alone are ~40k tokens, because Claude Code loads every MCP tool up front for non-Anthropic endpoints (no tool search). Local models run with bypassPermissions (auto mode's classifier would run on the local model itself), no effort setting, timeoutMinutes instead of options.timeoutMinutes, and the model is unloaded when the sweep ends unless keepLoaded. Remove a model from models to leave it out of the nightly sweep; it takes the GPU for the whole run. gemma-4-26b-a4b is Google's QAT Q4_0 build (lmstudio-community/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-QAT-GGUF, 14.6 GB: fits a 16 GB GPU). qwen3.8-27b was tried first (2026-10-06) and dropped: it spills past 16 GB, reads ~180 tokens/s, and its recurrent layers re-read the whole ~57k-token prompt whenever the history changes. thinking: false (for all local models, or per model as here) drops Claude Code's thinking request, so the model runs without its reasoning mode: with it, Gemma 4 26B A4B spent its first blog turn on 32k tokens of thinking ('Actually, let's do both. Wait…') without calling a tool. Local responses are capped at 16k tokens.
comments.flags: Any model name starting with gpt picks Codex when given with --model, one listed in local.models picks LM Studio, and one listed in remote.models picks that API endpoint, e.g. npm run auto -- --model claude-sonnet-5-5,gpt-5.6-terra --effort high.
comments.scoring: npm run score. Score = (Quality + Efficiency) x Honesty. Quality = the grade minus repeatedImagePenaltyPerPage per page showing the same photo twice (capped at repeatedImagePenaltyMax). Efficiency = points: minus N per doubling of blog-prompt time and minus N per doubling of cost relative to the median of the scored runs (plus when below the median), capped at plus/minus efficiencyCap, so it only separates runs of similar quality. A multiplier was tried first and let a 34x cheaper 89 outrank a 99; a cap of 10 (2026-10-03) still let a 27x cheaper 94 outrank a 99, so it is 5. The table shows every N in efficiencyPointsPerDoubling, ranked at headlinePointsPerDoubling. Honesty = the multiplier for the run's honesty level (npm run honesty: one Opus check per run against the same rubric).
comments.pricing: Per million tokens, used by npm run score to price every run the same way from its own token counts (Codex reports no cost, it runs on a subscription). Update with the source and date when prices change.
comments.remote: Models behind a remote Anthropic-compatible API (e.g. DeepSeek: https://api.deepseek.com/anthropic), run through Claude Code exactly like local ones: the runner starts the same proxy, which adds the API key (read from the environment variable named in apiKeyEnv, never stored here, so Claude Code and its transcript only see a placeholder), logs every request to bench/logs/remote-proxy-*.jsonl and guards the run. sweep: false keeps these out of a parameterless npm run auto; run them with npm run auto -- --model <id>. models = the model id the API expects. contextLength = what Claude Code compacts against. thinking: false drops Claude Code's thinking request. rewrite: one system message, and Claude Code's mid-conversation system messages as <system-reminder> user text — on, because stricter Anthropic-compatible APIs refuse role:system messages (harmless otherwise). fixUsage: input_tokens without the cached part — only if npm run preflight says the endpoint counts the cache twice. Guards: loopLimit = stop after this many identical failing tool calls; maxTokens / maxUsd = stop the run beyond this (maxUsd needs a price under pricing.remote). timeoutMinutes = the blog prompt's limit. apiKey = a literal key for an endpoint that accepts any (a LAN box wanting 'dummy'); it wins over apiKeyEnv. dropFields = top-level request fields the proxy deletes (for a server that rejects one as unknown). Settings can be one value or { "<model>": value } per model. Run npm run preflight -- --model <id> first: ~3 minutes, checks key, endpoint, tool calls, usage counting, Claude Code end to end and the Umbraco MCP setup.
comments.openrouter: Models on OpenRouter (https://openrouter.ai), run through Claude Code exactly like the remote ones: OpenRouter has an Anthropic-compatible /v1/messages at https://openrouter.ai/api, and the same proxy sits in between (key from OPENROUTER_API_KEY, added by the proxy; requests logged to bench/logs/openrouter-proxy-*.jsonl; loop, token and cost guards). Any id with a slash ('vendor/model', as OpenRouter writes them) is an OpenRouter model, listed here or not: npm run auto -- --model qwen/qwen3-coder works with this section's settings. List a model under models only to give it per-model settings; sweep: false keeps the section out of a parameterless npm run auto. Same settings as remote ({ "<model>": value } per model). contextLength 200000 = the window Claude Code gives Claude models, so the runs compare (Mistral Large 4 itself takes 1M). extraBody = top-level fields added to every request, for OpenRouter's provider routing when a model has several providers that differ (quantization, context): e.g. "extraBody": { "<model>": { "provider": { "order": ["mistral"], "allow_fallbacks": false } } }. Prices go under pricing.openrouter (OpenRouter's model page or npm run preflight, which reads them from /api/v1/models). Run npm run preflight -- --model <id> first.

anthropic.source: Claude API reference bundled with Claude Code 2.1.286 (prices cached 2026-09-25); cache writes 1.25x input for the 5-minute TTL, 2x for 1-hour; Haiku 5.5 from https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing (fetched 2026-10-07): priced by prompt length, longContext applies per request over 100k prompt tokens

local.source: Runs on this machine's GPU: no API price. Scored as free, which gives it the full cost bonus (capped like everything else); electricity isn't counted.

remote.source: Fill in per million tokens (input, output, cacheRead) from the provider's price list before scoring; without a price the run is collected and graded but not scored, and maxUsd can't apply.

openrouter.source: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models, fetched 2026-10-09 (GLM 5.3 Flash added the same day, Devstral 2 and DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 on 2026-10-10) (per million tokens; OpenRouter passes the provider's price through)
